meta.title: Use of Spill Control Kit in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To safely contain, neutralize, and clean up chemical or biological spills in the Pharmacognosy laboratory to minimize health hazards, environmental contamination, and damage to laboratory infrastructure.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for management of spills of organic solvents (methanol, ethanol, petroleum ether), acid/base solutions, and herbal extract concentrates.
procedure: In case of a spill, immediately alert all persons in the laboratory and evacuate the immediate area if the spill involves volatile or toxic solvents.
Do not attempt to clean up if you are not trained — wait for a trained spill responder.
Identify the spilled material using the container label or Safety Data Sheet (SDS) before selecting cleanup materials.
Put on appropriate PPE before approaching the spill: nitrile gloves, safety goggles, lab coat, and solvent-resistant apron for organic solvents.
Locate the spill control kit — it should be stored at a clearly marked, accessible location in each laboratory.
For flammable solvent spills: Eliminate all ignition sources (flames, sparks) immediately; increase ventilation.
Contain the spill by placing absorbent socks or sand/vermiculite around the perimeter of the spill to prevent spreading.
Apply absorbent granules (general purpose absorbent) generously over the spill from the outer edge toward the centre.
Allow absorbents to soak up the liquid completely (typically 5–10 minutes).
Using a plastic scoop (never metal for flammable materials), collect the used absorbent into a yellow hazardous waste bag.
Wipe the area with absorbent wipes until clean; for corrosive spills, neutralize before final wipe (use sodium bicarbonate for acid spills; citric acid/boric acid for base spills).
Place all used materials (gloves, wipes, absorbents) in the hazardous waste bag and seal.
Label the waste bag with: spill material, date, quantity, and handler's name.
Hand over the sealed waste bag to the designated chemical waste disposal officer.
Replenish the spill kit immediately after use — a depleted spill kit is a compliance violation.
Complete an incident report form within 24 hours of the spill.
precautions: Never use paper towels for solvent spills — they provide no absorbency advantage and are a fire hazard.
Never use wet mops on organic solvent spills — spreading increases the vapor surface area.
Eliminate all ignition sources before cleaning flammable solvent spills.
Do not use metal scoops or tools near flammable liquid spills — risk of static spark.
For large spills (> 4 litres) or spills of toxic/carcinogenic materials, evacuate and call emergency services.
Inspect the spill kit monthly — check that all absorbents, PPE, and bags are present and undamaged.
Know the location of the emergency eyewash station and safety shower before starting any experiment.
All laboratory staff must be trained in spill response procedures — training records must be maintained.
